html:
The Second Polish Republic was the Polish state from 1918 to 1939, reborn on 11 November 1918 when Józef Piłsudski took command in Warsaw as Germany, Austria and Russia collapsed at the end of World War I.

Its borders were set by war: with Ukrainians in Galicia, with Germans in Silesia, and with Soviet Russia, beaten at the Battle of Warsaw in 1920. About a third of its people were minorities, Ukrainians, Jews, Belarusians and Germans. It built a new port at Gdynia and united three legal systems. In 1926 Piłsudski took power in a coup and ruled until his death in 1935. It ended with the German and Soviet invasion of 1939. 11 November is Independence Day in Poland.
sum: The Second Polish Republic was the Polish state from 1918 to 1939, reborn on 11 November 1918 when Józef Piłsudski took command in Warsaw as Germany, Austria and Russia collapsed at the end of World War I.
